candidates.label: Developmental mental health and clinical assessment
candidates.reason: The broad route already contains the same abnormal, lifespan, health, diagnostic and youth psychology. Four alternative biomedical/public-health/ethics courses do not add a sustained distinct clinical psychology direction; withdrawn without implying clinical qualification.

candidates.label: Psychology in education and schools
candidates.reason: Lifespan development and Youth Resilience supply real developmental and school-prevention substance; Rhetoric in Action supplies community-engaged school pedagogy, and Leading Under Pressure contributes belonging/inclusion and psychological measurement. These useful elements are already in the retained routes, especially the social route. A proposed school direction would reuse that same developmental/social/prevention/communication set rather than establish a sustained distinct programme of learning, educational assessment and school intervention. The current psychology/cognition pool was examined without excluding description-only courses. Not rejected merely for lacking a teaching credential.

candidates.label: Neurorehabilitation and recovery of cognitive function
candidates.reason: Actual neurobiology, cognitive functions, perception and language offer substantive cognitive study, already in the closest route. They do not supply sustained rehabilitation assessment, recovery or intervention study. No distinct rehabilitation concept is established by adjacent neuroscience alone; absence of a professional title or licence is not the rejection criterion.

stopping.assessment: Two coherent substantial responses retained. The clinical candidate duplicates the primary psychology core; its biomedical substitutions do not establish distinct clinical study. Education and rehabilitation candidates lack sustained defining content. No third alternative is justified.

conceptReview.closest: Sustained neural/cognitive/social/developmental/clinical psychology and actual psychological methods provide a material response to the target’s defining substance. General cell biology supports biological foundations but is not counted as psychology. Philosophy, rhetoric and sociology remain complementary; clinical assessment or cognitive study is not professional registration.
conceptReview.social: Organisational psychology plus actual emotion/inclusion survey work and social, clinical and developmental psychology support the related organisational concept. Leadership/rhetoric/negotiation/literary stylistics remain complementary applications. The new Leading Under Pressure profile materially strengthens actual psychological research, not a reason to reclassify every leadership course as psychology.
conceptReview.distinctness: Eight exclusive courses/60EC per route,16shared. Cognitive/neurobiological/perception/language/health/philosophy versus sustained organisations,leadership,negotiation andcommunication. Substantive priorities produce the differences.
conceptReview.schoolAndRehabilitation: Reviewed all current psychology/cognition offerings and school-related selected evidence. Lifespan, youth prevention, school rhetoric and belonging support useful applications already in retained routes, especially the social route; they do not establish a further substantively distinct school programme. Brain/perception/language cannot establish a recovery/intervention sequence. No rejection rests solely on a degree title, licence or planning absence.

courseEvidence.description2: This course is a first-year requirement and aims to stimulate personal development, namely, being able to actively, consciously and ethically orientate oneself in relation to others and the world. It supports the development of core personal and academic skills that enhance critical thinking and independent learning. It seeks to improve and develop academic writing and presenting skills and helps students develop the foundational skills and attitudes to reflect on societal issues and engage with societal partners.

Students locate and evaluate scholarly sources, synthesize literature, formulate research questions and arguments, and construct a research-paper introduction. A community-engaged project with a societal partner connects these skills to collaboration, reflection and practical contribution. Personal development planning addresses learning goals, self-efficacy, and stress and time management; the course also considers responsible academic use of AI.

courseEvidence.description2: Research Methods & Statistics gives you a strong foundation in how business management—and social and behavioral sciences—move from mere practices to true fields of scientific study. You’ll learn how to plan research logically, from designing studies to working with real data using experimental and survey techniques. You’ll also study descriptive and inferential statistics, with a brief intro to multivariate tools.

R and R Commander support data display and analysis. Project teams develop instruments and a research plan, collect and analyze data, and report results under explicit research-ethics and privacy requirements.

courseEvidence.description2: Psycholinguistics is the study of the neurobiological and psychological factors that enable us to acquire, use, and understand language. Modern research draws on cognitive psychology, neuroscience, and computer science to investigate how language is processed. The course focuses primarily, though not exclusively, on the neuroscience of language. Students examine theoretical and experimental issues in speech production and comprehension, language impairments, the relationship between thought and language, and the evolution and acquisition of language. They also gain hands-on experience with experimental approaches to the study of language and develop an understanding of human linguistic capacity as a subject of multidisciplinary research. Topics covered: What is language? Evolutionary aspects of language and animal communication; language and thought; aphasia; language acquisition; bilingualism; speech comprehension; semantics; reading and dyslexia; speech production.

courseEvidence.description2: What does it take to lead effectively through pressure, conflict, and diversity? Explore how emotion, identity, belonging, and inclusion shape leadership, teamwork, and performance. Design and conduct an original empirical study while building career-ready skills in research design, data analysis, teamwork, ethical decision-making, and scientific communication.
courseEvidence.name: Psychology of Leading Under Pressure
courseEvidence.profile: Examines how emotion regulation, emotional intelligence, emotional expression and suppression, emotional labor, belonging, identity safety and psychological safety shape leadership and social interaction under conflict, exclusion and interpersonal uncertainty. It emphasises inclusive leadership and ethnic, cultural, sexual and gender minority experiences, with digital emotion regulation as a further strand. Students conduct a supervised quantitative survey project: formulating theory-driven hypotheses, selecting established psychological measures, designing and piloting a Qualtrics survey, recruiting participants ethically, collecting original data and preparing a clean dataset. Individual work applies descriptive statistics, reliability analysis, correlations, group comparisons and introductory multiple regression in SPSS or RStudio, and interprets findings and limitations in empirical reports and evidence-based leadership recommendations.

courseEvidence.methods: Theory-driven hypothesis formulation; Quantitative survey research; Established psychological measure selection and evaluation; Qualtrics survey construction and piloting; Ethical participant recruitment and original data collection; Codebook development, reverse coding and scale scoring; Data cleaning and missing-data documentation; Descriptive statistics; Reliability analysis; Correlation analysis; Group comparisons; Introductory multiple regression in SPSS or RStudio; APA-style empirical reporting

courseEvidence.description2: Develops persuasive speaking skills by applying rhetorical theory in the real world. Students work with local primary school children, building public-speaking skills and empowering them to find their voices.
courseEvidence.name: Rhetoric in Action
courseEvidence.profile: Applies rhetoric through community-engaged work with local primary-school children. Students develop their own public-speaking, debating and storytelling skills, then design and iteratively refine age-appropriate teaching activities with school partners. On-site coaching and a final public-speaking event connect rhetorical education to civic participation and confidence. Structured reflection examines reciprocity, cultural sensitivity, personal development and the practical challenges of community-engaged teaching.
